notes: Hook checked: a bank that shows a healthy voltage on float yet falls short on its discharge test is supported by the research (capacity test is the only way to get an accurate value on actual capacity [49]; replacement below 80% capacity [45]) and by lesson i1 (a healthy rested voltage reflects the plate materials and acid strength, not how much plate material can still react). It is posed as a question, not answered, so it stands.

Now: 'too high and they corrode, and near full charge the cells give off hydrogen the room must clear'.

oneBreath narrowed: 'the acid is used up' became 'much of the acid is used up' (research [4]: 'highly consumed'; a flat cell still holds weak acid), and 'its tiny resistance' became 'a large battery's tiny resistance', matching idea i8 and research [51]-[53].
